The glaring absence is Claude: Anthropic refused to strip out its safety limits, got frozen out, sued, and last week a federal judge actually called the government's move against them illegal and baseless.

Worth watching if you build on these models — the safety-versus-access fight just landed in a courtroom.

On the useful front, Anthropic also rolled out shared memory across your chats and its Cowork mode, so an assistant can genuinely pick a task back up where you left it.

— personal items —

With thirty-six degrees on tap, keep a bottle within reach and drink before you're thirsty; the dry heat hides how much you're losing.

Two to finish.

Word of the day: sonder — that quiet jolt when you realize every stranger you pass has a life as deep and messy as your own.

As in, the metro at rush hour is pure sonder.

And a productivity nudge: give a task a hard deadline, not just a start time.

Parkinson's Law says work swells to fill whatever time you allow it, so telling yourself something gets one hour often means it's actually done in one.
